variants.subject: a one-pager for {company}
variants.body:
Hi {greeting},

No pitch, just something useful.

Reply REVIEW and I send you a written one-pager on the AI feature {company} is building: the stack I would pick, the three biggest risks, a realistic timeline, and the eval template we start every build with. No call attached.

Why it is worth reading: I am on the engineering team at Diraya. We help seed to Series B teams ship a working AI feature in 8 weeks with a written eval suite, not 6 months of demos. One fintech we worked with went from a brittle demo to passing a 300-case eval suite in 8 weeks, then kept shipping on the repo we handed over.

If the one-pager is useful and you want to talk, the call is there. If not, it is yours either way.

P.s. if you would rather just see where agents break, reply GHOSTS for our list of 40 production-killer edge cases, each with the failure mode and the eval that catches it. Free, no call.

variants.subject: 8 weeks for {company}
variants.body:
Hi {greeting},

Follow up on the AI feature point.

The specific path I am thinking for {company}: week 1 we write the eval suite together, week 2 the first milestone ships, weeks 3 to 8 we build out the agent and harden it against the evals. Day 56 you own the repo.

The price is fixed before we start. The first milestone lands on day 14 or you owe nothing and walk with what we have built.

15 minutes this week to scope what that looks like for you? Grab a time that works here: https://calendly.com/amoura-ma-diraya/30min

P.s. the Ghost-Cases List is still yours if you want it. Reply GHOSTS.

variants.subject: 0.4 percent
variants.body:
Hi {greeting},

One number.

0.4 percent. Last health tech build we did, that is where the hallucination rate landed after 8 weeks. Started at 12 percent. The agent now answers patient-facing queries in production and their support team stopped manually checking outputs.

The path was not magic. It was: build the eval suite first, then the agent, then iterate against the evals until the number was low enough to ship.

The same pattern would work for {company}. The eval suite is the lever. Most teams skip it and that is why their agents look great in demo and break in production.

15 minutes to look at what your eval suite would need to cover?

P.s. happy to do this for you for free. Reply REVIEW and within 48 hours I send a written one-pager on the AI feature {company} is building: the stack I would pick, the three biggest risks, a realistic timeline, plus the eval template we start every build with. No call attached.

variants.subject: you are busy, here is the math
variants.body:
Hi {greeting},

Fourth email, you are clearly heads-down shipping. Last note from me before I switch to give-only mode.

Here is the math on why I keep writing.

If {company} delays the AI feature by 3 months while a competitor ships it, that gap compounds. Your team loses interview wins, your sales team loses the answer to 'do you have AI', and your roadmap loses 3 months you do not get back.

If {company} ships in 8 weeks instead of 6 months, the gap goes the other way.

The offer is: working code on day 14 or you owe nothing. Fixed scope, fixed price, full handover to your team. The downside is 15 minutes on a call. The upside is 4 months of compounding ahead of the people who keep promising AI without shipping it.

Reply with a time or a no. Either one lets me move on cleanly.

P.s. still happy to send the Ghost-Cases List with no call. Reply GHOSTS.

variants.subject: {greeting}, yes or no
variants.body:
Hi {greeting},

Clean question.

If Diraya could ship a production AI feature for {company} in 8 weeks with a written eval suite and full handover, and the first milestone landed on day 14 or you walked with no invoice and the code we had built so far, would you say yes to a 15-minute call?

A clear yes or a clear no. Either one is the right answer for me. If it is a yes, the fastest path is to grab a slot here: https://calendly.com/amoura-ma-diraya/30min

P.s. if it is a no on the build, the Ghost-Cases List and the architecture review are still on the table. Reply GHOSTS or REVIEW.

variants.subject: two things you can use whether we work together or not
variants.body:

Switching to give-only mode as promised.

No call, no obligation, no follow-up sequence after this. Take either or both.

variants.subject: closing your file at Diraya
variants.body:
Hi {greeting},

Closing your file at Diraya today. We take a small number of new builds per quarter and the next slots are filling.

Three last things:

If the timing was wrong, that is fine. Tell me when the right window is and I will reach back out then.

If the offer was wrong, tell me what would have landed and I will listen. I read every reply.

If nothing was right, no hard feelings. The Ghost-Cases List and the free architecture review are still yours, no call attached. Just reply GHOSTS or REVIEW.

Good luck with what you are building.
